Colors.Blend.Tip.message:
How this row's art combines with what is already on the skin.

"Paint" lays it on top, which is what every layer has always done.
Anything else makes this row a PRINT: it colours the fabric this mod's
other layers painted, and is clipped to their shape — so a rainbow on a
fishnet colours the threads and leaves the holes as skin.

A print only reaches its OWN mod's layers; it never touches another mod's
clothing. On bare skin it paints nothing at all, so a print selected on its
own shows nothing — there is nothing there to print on.

Multiply can only darken, so it reads faintly on very dark fabric — use
Screen there instead. This row's colour still tints the art, and its
Opacity is the print's strength.
Colors.Blend.Tip.description: Tooltip on the Blend dropdown. "Paint", "Multiply" and "Screen" are mode names - translate them the same way as the Colors.Blend.* entries above. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.

Colors.OneSided.Tip.message:
Turn this on for art meant to appear on ONE side only — a tattoo on one arm, a scar on
one cheek. Leave it off for anything else, including ordinary skin.
A vanilla body and the vanilla face give both sides the same pixels, so art painted for
them is folded in half: one side is kept and mirrored across. That is invisible on a
symmetric design and ruins a one-sided one. With this on, Proteus renders the overlay
through a layer of its own whose two sides read the two halves of your sheet, so both
sides survive.
It cannot be detected for you. Real skin is never symmetric — freckles and moles differ
left to right — so only you can say whether a difference is the point or just detail.

1.00 keeps the authored colour on any skin tone — right for fabric that covers the skin.
0.00 lets the skin tone through — right for a tattoo, a decal, or a body texture that IS skin.
The global slider in Settings multiplies this, so 0.00 here always wins.

Colors.WholeSkin.Tip.message:
Turn this on for a converted skin mod — art that IS the skin, not something laid on it.
It moves two settings together, and they only work as a pair.
The normal REPLACES the one already on the material instead of being added to it. Off is
right for a strap or a tattoo, which should keep the skin's pores underneath; for a skin
the map underneath is that same skin, so adding lands every pore twice and the body goes
flat against an untouched face, with a hard line at the neck seam.
And skin-tint suppression drops to 0.00, so the wearer's tone comes through — it exists
to stop fabric being re-tinted, which is backwards for skin. Turning this off restores
both. You can still set the slider by hand afterwards.
Colors.WholeSkin.Tip.description: Tooltip for the checkbox above. "normal" is the normal map (a texture). "0.00" is a numeric value - keep the digits. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.

Create.FaceSplit.Tip.message:
Tick this only for a face texture painted as TWO HALVES: the character's right side in the right half of the image, their left side in the left half.
An ordinary face texture gives both cheeks the same pixels, so a mark on one side alone cannot exist in it — Proteus renders a split one through a face layer instead.
Leave this off for any normal face texture.

Create.Glow.Always.description: Radio button label in the Create tab.

Create.Glow.Always.Tip.message:
The tattoo is there in daylight and glows day and night.
Kept gentle on purpose: this shader adds one flat colour across the whole tattoo
rather than following the picture, so a strong value bleaches the art in daylight.
For a brighter glow at night without that, raise Glow in Colors and set "Fades in light".
Create.Glow.Always.Tip.description: Tooltip. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number.

Create.Glow.DarkOnly.description: Radio button label in the Create tab.

Create.Glow.DarkOnly.Tip.message:
Nothing in daylight, glowing in an unlit room — what Atramentum Luminis tattoos did.
The art fades out as the light on you rises, and takes its own surface with it, so
there's skin and nothing else in the bright.
Needs "React to the scene's light" in Settings, which is on by default.
Create.Glow.DarkOnly.Tip.description: Tooltip. "Atramentum Luminis" is the name of an older FFXIV shader mod - keep it as-is. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number.

Create.Glow.Label.description: Checkbox label in the Create tab.

Create.Glow.NeedsDiffuse.message: Pick a diffuse texture first — the glow takes its colour from the art.
Create.Glow.NeedsDiffuse.description: Tooltip shown when the glow checkbox is disabled because no diffuse texture is picked.

Create.Glow.NeedsSkin.message:
Only skin and face targets can glow. A glowing overlay is drawn on a second skin cut
from your body, and there's nothing to cut one from on gear, an accessory or a weapon.
Create.Glow.NeedsSkin.description: Tooltip shown when the glow checkbox is disabled because the material target isn't skin or a face. Contains a deliberate line break.

Create.Glow.Tip.message:
Light the art up. Its colour comes from the picture itself, per pixel — there is
nothing else to set.
Skin can't emit, so a glowing overlay renders on a second skin instead of being
painted into yours. Everything else about it works the same, and the Glow dial in
Colors adjusts it afterwards.

Create.WholeSkin.Tip.message:
Tick this when you're converting a full skin mod, not painting something onto skin.
Proteus ticks it for you when the textures look like one; your own answer always wins.
Three things follow. The normal REPLACES the one already on the material instead of
stacking onto it — otherwise it lands on top of the same map underneath, every pore
and crease is applied twice, and the body reads flat against the face with a hard line
at the neck seam. Skin-tint suppression goes off, so the wearer's skin tone comes
through: it is there to stop fabric being re-tinted, and this art IS the skin. And
"Bodies" is set to "All bodies", so the skin reaches a vanilla body as well.
Create.WholeSkin.Tip.description: Tooltip for the checkbox above. "normal" is the normal map (a texture). The two quoted names are UI labels - use exactly your translations of Colors.Bodies.Label and Colors.Bodies.All so the tooltip names the control the user sees. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.

Eye.Cutout.Artwork.description: The other choice in the glow-shape combo: confine the glow to the drawn shape, dropping the fade around it.

Eye.Cutout.Falloff.description: One of two choices in the glow-shape combo: keep the soft fade the artist drew around the artwork.

Eye.Cutout.Label.description: Label of the combo choosing how much of the mask becomes the glowing shape. Keep it short; the "###" suffix is a widget id and must be left exactly as it is.

Eye.Cutout.Tip.message:
How much of the mask's glow channel is cut into the shape that glows. Most packs mark the artwork brightly and fade out around it; keeping that falloff glows softly beyond the artwork, dropping it confines the glow to the shape itself.
Baked in at import, so pick it now — afterwards the Glow dial can only scale what's left.
Eye.Cutout.Tip.description: Tooltip for the glow-shape combo. "Glow" is the name of a dial in this plugin's Colors tab.

Eye.FallbackIrises.message: Proteus couldn't read the game's face list, so the glow will target a known-good pair of faces only. Reopen this pack once you're in game to pick up every race.
Eye.FallbackIrises.description: Amber note in the Import tab: the game data could not be read, so the glow will only reach two faces. "Proteus" is the plugin name.

Eye.Glow.Fmt.message: The mask marks {0:P1} of the sheet as glowing, and that shape gets the animation — on {1} iris material(s), so it follows you across races and faces. Switch it off under "{2}" in Penumbra.
Eye.Glow.Fmt.description: Plain (not amber) line before the Import button, saying what the glow will do. {0} is a fraction shown as a percentage by the "P1" specifier, which must be kept; {1} a count of iris materials; {2} the Penumbra option group's name. "Penumbra" is a plugin name.

Eye.Intro.message: Import an eye texture pack (.zip of loose images). Its eyes go in as normal, and the shape its mask marks out gets an animated glow you can recolour and dim.
Eye.Intro.description: One of four bullets introducing the Import tab, in the same voice as the others: what you get, not how it works.

Eye.NoGlow.message: No animated glow will be added — see below. The eye textures still import and work normally.
Eye.NoGlow.description: Plain line before the Import button when no animated glow can be added. The reasons follow it in amber.

Eye.NothingUsable.message: Nothing in this archive looks like an eye texture.
Eye.NothingUsable.description: Tooltip on the disabled Import button when the archive holds nothing that looks like an eye texture.

Eye.ReadFailed.Fmt.description: Shown when the picked .zip could not be read at all. {0} is the reader's own reason and arrives in English.

Eye.Skipped.description: Table cell marking a file that will not be imported; the reason is in its tooltip. Keep it very short and lower case.

Eye.SkippedReason.Fmt.description: Tooltip on a skipped file. {0} is its name and {1} the reason, a sentence fragment beginning in lower case.

Eye.TextureCount.Fmt.description: Header above the file table. {0} is how many will be imported, {1} how many the archive holds.

Footer.SecondsAgo.Fmt.description: {0} is an already-formatted number. Very tight space.

Import.AsTex.Tip.message:
Roughly a quarter of the disk size, and no PNG decode at composite time.
Block compression is lossy — leave it off to keep the pack's images exactly as authored.
Import.AsTex.Tip.description: Tooltip. Appears in the Import tab. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.

Import.AsTex.Unavailable.Tip.message: The native block compressor isn't loaded, so BC7 encoding would take minutes.
Import.AsTex.Unavailable.Tip.description: Tooltip. Appears in the Import tab.

Import.Author.Label.description: Control label. Appears in the Import tab.

Import.BodyFit.NotDrawn.Fmt.message: Your character isn't drawn yet, so Proteus picked "{0}" by preference rather than by your body. Check the result once you're in game.
Import.BodyFit.NotDrawn.Fmt.description: Appears in the Import tab. Takes arguments - keep every {0}, {1} ... exactly once; you may reorder them.

Import.BodyFit.Remapped.Fmt.message: This pack has nothing for your {0} body, so "{1}" will be remapped onto it automatically.
Import.BodyFit.Remapped.Fmt.description: Appears in the Import tab. Takes arguments - keep every {0}, {1} ... exactly once; you may reorder them.

Import.Browse.Btn.description: Button caption. Appears in the Import tab.

Import.DefaultLayoutMatched.Fmt.message: "{0}" will be selected — it matches the body you're wearing.
Import.DefaultLayoutMatched.Fmt.description: Appears in the Import tab. Takes arguments - keep every {0}, {1} ... exactly once; you may reorder them.

Import.Dialog.Filter.description: Human half of the file picker's filter; the braced extension list is appended in code.

Import.Dialog.Title.description: Title of the file picker. One dialog now offers both pack formats.

Import.Emissive.Description.Fmt.message: Imported from the emissive skin pack "{0}".

Import.Emissive.Fail.BadName.message: That mod name has no usable characters — use letters or numbers.

Import.Emissive.Fail.NoModDir.description: Emissive skin import: refused because Penumbra's mod directory could not be read.

Import.Emissive.Fail.NothingUsable.message: Nothing in this pack can be imported.

Import.Emissive.Fail.Reserved.message: "Proteus" is reserved — choose a different mod name.
Import.Emissive.Fail.Reserved.description: Emissive skin import: refused because "Proteus" is the managed output mod's own folder.

Import.Emissive.Fail.Write.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: the write failed. {0} is the exception's message.

Import.Emissive.Option.Glow.description: Emissive skin import: the Penumbra option name when the pack ships one picture.

Import.Emissive.Option.GlowFor.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: the Penumbra option name when the pack ships one picture per body layout. {0} is the body, e.g. "bibo".

Import.Emissive.Result.NoSelection.Fmt.message: Imported "{0}" — textures: {1}{2}, but Proteus couldn't switch it on for you. Tick it under "{3}" in Penumbra, or nothing will paint.
Import.Emissive.Result.NoSelection.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: the mod is in but Proteus could not tick its option. {0} is the mod folder, {1} the texture count, {2} an optional " (skipped: n)" tail, {3} the Penumbra group name.

Import.Emissive.Result.Ok.Fmt.message: Imported "{0}" — textures: {1}{2}. The glow is on and needs no shader mod. Recolour or dim it in Colors, or switch it off under "{3}" in Penumbra.
Import.Emissive.Result.Ok.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: success. {0} is the mod folder, {1} the texture count, {2} an optional " (skipped: n)" tail, {3} the Penumbra group name. "Colors" is a Proteus tab name.

Import.Emissive.Skip.Missing.Fmt.message: the pack's manifest names it but the archive doesn't contain "{0}".
Import.Emissive.Skip.Missing.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: skipped because the pack's manifest names a file the archive does not contain. {0} is the missing archive entry.

Import.Emissive.Skip.NoGlow.message: its alpha channel is empty, so it marks nothing as glowing. An emissive map puts the shape of the glow there, and one without a shape is not a tattoo.
Import.Emissive.Skip.NoGlow.description: Emissive skin import: skipped because the emissive map's alpha channel marks nothing as glowing.

Import.Emissive.Skip.TooSmall.Fmt.message: it is only {0}×{1}, which is a shader's effect or palette map rather than art painted on a body.
Import.Emissive.Skip.TooSmall.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: skipped because the texture is far too small to be body art — it is the shader's effect or palette map. {0} and {1} are its width and height.

Import.Emissive.Skip.Undecodable.description: Emissive skin import: skipped because the texture's pixels could not be decoded.

Import.Emissive.Skip.UnknownBody.Fmt.message: Proteus doesn't know the body "{0}", and can't ask your character which one they are wearing until they're drawn. Load in and reopen this pack.
Import.Emissive.Skip.UnknownBody.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: skipped because Proteus knows neither the pack's body token nor the one the character is wearing. {0} is the token.

Import.Emissive.Warn.FromWearer.Fmt.message: Proteus doesn't know this pack's body layout, so it will paint the art onto the body you're wearing ({0}) exactly as it is, with no resizing. If the pack was painted for a different body it will look wrong — change the body target below if you know better.
Import.Emissive.Warn.FromWearer.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: warning that the pack's body layout is unknown, so the art is aimed at the body the character is wearing. {0} is that body's material suffix.

Import.Emissive.Warn.MostlyGlow.Fmt.message: "{0}" glows across {1:P0} of the body. That is legal, but it usually means the texture has no real alpha channel — check the result before wearing it out.
Import.Emissive.Warn.MostlyGlow.Fmt.description: Emissive skin import: warning that a texture glows almost everywhere, which usually means it has no real alpha channel. {0} is its path, {1} the fraction — keep the percent format.

Import.Emissive.Warn.NothingImportable.message: Nothing in this pack can be imported — see the reasons above.
Import.Emissive.Warn.NothingImportable.description: Emissive skin import: warning that nothing in the pack can be imported.

Import.Eye.Description.Fmt.message: Imported from the eye texture pack "{0}".
Import.Eye.Description.Fmt.description: Written into the imported mod's Penumbra description. {0} is the .zip file name.

Import.Eye.Fail.BadName.message: That mod name has no usable characters — use letters or numbers.
Import.Eye.Fail.BadName.description: The import was refused before anything was written: the mod name is punctuation only.

Import.Eye.Fail.Exists.Fmt.message: A mod folder named "{0}" already exists.
Import.Eye.Fail.Exists.Fmt.description: The import was refused: {0} is a mod folder name already in Penumbra's mod directory.

Import.Eye.Fail.Gone.Fmt.message: The archive is no longer there: {0}
Import.Eye.Fail.Gone.Fmt.description: The import was refused: {0} is the .zip path, moved or deleted since it was picked.

Import.Eye.Fail.NoModDir.description: The import was refused because Penumbra did not answer with its mod directory. "Penumbra" is a plugin name.

Import.Eye.Fail.NoneWritten.message: None of this archive's textures could be read, so nothing was written.
Import.Eye.Fail.NoneWritten.description: The import failed after the fact: not one texture could be decoded, so the mod folder was rolled back.

Import.Eye.Fail.NothingUsable.message: Nothing in this archive can be imported.
Import.Eye.Fail.NothingUsable.description: The import was refused: no file in the archive is a recognisable eye texture.

Import.Eye.Fail.Reserved.message: "Proteus" is reserved — choose a different mod name.
Import.Eye.Fail.Reserved.description: The import was refused: "Proteus" is the plugin's own managed folder. The quoted word is a folder name, not prose.

Import.Eye.Fail.Write.Fmt.description: The import failed part-way and was rolled back. {0} is the underlying error, which arrives in English from the operating system.

Import.Eye.Option.Glow.description: Name of the Penumbra option that switches the animated glow on. Shown in Penumbra's own option list, so keep it short.

Import.Eye.Result.NoGlow.Fmt.message: Imported "{0}" — textures: {1}, but with no animated glow. See the reasons above; the eyes themselves are in and working.
Import.Eye.Result.NoGlow.Fmt.description: Amber result line: the eye textures imported but no animation could be added. {0} mod folder name, {1} texture count.

Import.Eye.Result.NotEnabled.Fmt.message: Imported "{0}" — textures: {1}. Penumbra hasn't switched it on yet; tick it in Penumbra's mod list.
Import.Eye.Result.NotEnabled.Fmt.description: Amber result line: the mod was written and added but Penumbra has not switched it on. {0} mod folder name, {1} texture count. "Penumbra" is a plugin name.

Import.Eye.Result.Ok.Fmt.message: Imported "{0}" — textures: {1}, with an animated glow on the shape the mask marks out. Tune it in Colors, or switch it off under "{2}" in Penumbra.
Import.Eye.Result.Ok.Fmt.description: Green result line after a successful import. {0} mod folder name, {1} texture count, {2} the Penumbra option group's name. "Colors" is a tab in this plugin.

Import.Eye.Skip.Duplicate.Fmt.message: another file in this archive is already the {0} texture.
Import.Eye.Skip.Duplicate.Fmt.description: Why one file was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. {0} is a texture kind (Base, Mask or Norm) and is not translated.

Import.Eye.Skip.NotEyes.message: this archive's names don't identify it as an eye pack, and Proteus won't point loose textures at your irises on a guess.
Import.Eye.Skip.NotEyes.description: Why a file was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. The archive's file names do not identify it as an eye pack.

Import.Eye.Skip.Unknown.message: its name doesn't end in a texture kind Proteus knows (base, mask or norm).
Import.Eye.Skip.Unknown.description: Why one file was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. The words base, mask and norm are file-name tokens and are not translated.

Import.Eye.Warn.FaceGuessed.Fmt.message: Your character isn't drawn, so the glow is being cut for face {0}. If you wear a different face, import this again once you're in game.
Import.Eye.Warn.FaceGuessed.Fmt.description: Amber warning in the Import tab. The glow is cut for one face id ({0}, e.g. "f0001", not translated) because a shell is resolved per face; the character was not drawn, so it was guessed.

Import.Eye.Warn.MaskUnreadable.message: The mask texture couldn't be decoded, so Proteus can't tell what should glow. The eye textures are still imported; only the glow is left out.
Import.Eye.Warn.MaskUnreadable.description: Amber warning in the Import tab: the mask image would not decode, so the glow region is unknown.

Import.Eye.Warn.NoGlowRegion.message: The mask's red channel is empty, so nothing in this pack is marked as glowing. That channel is where the game reads the limbal ring from, and where a glowing eye mod puts its shape. The eye textures are still imported; only the glow is left out.
Import.Eye.Warn.NoGlowRegion.description: Amber warning in the Import tab: the mask's red channel is empty. That channel is where the game reads the limbal ring from.

Import.Eye.Warn.NoIrisMaterials.message: Proteus couldn't read the game's face list, so it has no iris material to put the glow on. The eye textures are still imported; only the glow is left out.
Import.Eye.Warn.NoIrisMaterials.description: Amber warning in the Import tab: the game's face list could not be read, so there is no iris material to put a glow on.

Import.Eye.Warn.NoMask.message: This pack ships no mask texture, so there is no shape for the animation to fill. The eye textures are still imported; only the glow is left out.
Import.Eye.Warn.NoMask.description: Amber warning in the Import tab: the pack ships no mask, so there is no shape for the animation to fill.

Import.Eye.Warn.NothingImportable.message: Nothing in this archive can be imported — see the reasons above.
Import.Eye.Warn.NothingImportable.description: Amber warning in the Import tab when every file in the archive was skipped.

Import.Failed.Fmt.description: Appears in the Import tab. Takes arguments - keep every {0}, {1} ... exactly once; you may reorder them.

Import.Import.Btn.description: Button caption. Appears in the Import tab.

Import.Importing.Btn.description: Button caption. Appears in the Import tab.

Import.Intro.message: Import an Onion overlay pack (.omp). Wear its layers as Proteus overlays you can recolour and restack.
Import.Intro.description: Second of the Import tab's two bulleted lines: what an .omp overlay pack gets you.

Import.Layer.SkippedReason.Fmt.description: {0} is a file name, {1} an English reason string produced by the importer. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.

Import.LayerCount.Fmt.description: {0} is how many layers will be imported, {1} the total in the pack.

Import.Layouts.Fmt.message: The pack has {0} UV layouts, so the mod gets a single-select "{1}" group in Penumbra ({2}). Only one composites at a time.
Import.Layouts.Fmt.description: {0} is a count, {1} is the Penumbra option-group name, {2} is a comma-joined list of layout names.

Import.Luminis.Description.Fmt.message: Imported from the Atramentum Luminis pack "{0}".
Import.Luminis.Description.Fmt.description: Written into the imported mod's Penumbra description. {0} is the .ttmp2 file name. "Atramentum Luminis" is the name of the older FFXIV shader mod these packs were made for; keep it as-is.

Import.Luminis.Fail.BadName.message: That mod name has no usable characters — use letters or numbers.
Import.Luminis.Fail.BadName.description: The import was refused before anything was written: the mod name is punctuation only.

Import.Luminis.Fail.Exists.Fmt.message: A mod folder named "{0}" already exists.
Import.Luminis.Fail.Exists.Fmt.description: The import was refused: {0} is a mod folder name already in Penumbra's mod directory.

Import.Luminis.Fail.Gone.Fmt.message: The pack is no longer there: {0}
Import.Luminis.Fail.Gone.Fmt.description: The import was refused: {0} is the .ttmp2 path, which has been moved or deleted since it was picked.

Import.Luminis.Fail.NoModDir.description: The import was refused because Penumbra did not answer with its mod directory. "Penumbra" is a plugin name and is not translated.

Import.Luminis.Fail.NoneWritten.message: None of this pack's textures could be read on the second pass, so nothing was written.
Import.Luminis.Fail.NoneWritten.description: The import was refused after the fact: every texture decoded during the preview and none of them would decode again during the write, so the mod was rolled back.

Import.Luminis.Fail.NothingUsable.message: Nothing in this pack can be imported.
Import.Luminis.Fail.NothingUsable.description: The import was refused: no texture in the modpack carries a glow mask.

Import.Luminis.Fail.Reserved.message: "Proteus" is reserved — choose a different mod name.
Import.Luminis.Fail.Reserved.description: The import was refused: "Proteus" is the plugin's own managed mod folder and cannot be reused. The quoted word is a folder name, not prose.

Import.Luminis.Fail.Write.Fmt.description: The import failed part-way and everything it wrote was rolled back. {0} is the underlying error, which arrives in English from the operating system.

Import.Luminis.Option.Glow.description: Name of the Penumbra option that switches the tattoo's glow on. Used when the pack has one picture; the .Fmt variant is used when it has several. Shown in Penumbra's own option list, so keep it short.

Import.Luminis.Option.Skin.description: Name of the Penumbra option that adds the pack author's own body texture under the glow. Arrives switched off. Shown in Penumbra's own option list, so keep it short.

Import.Luminis.Option.SkinOf.Fmt.description: Name of the Penumbra option that adds one picture's underlying body texture, when the pack ships several. {0} is the texture's own name. Shown in Penumbra's option list, so keep it short.

Import.Luminis.Result.NoSelection.Fmt.message: Imported "{0}" — textures: {1}{2}, but Proteus couldn't switch it on for you. Tick it under "{3}" in Penumbra, or nothing will paint.
Import.Luminis.Result.NoSelection.Fmt.description: Amber result line: the mod imported but Penumbra refused the option selection, so nothing renders until the user ticks it. {0} mod folder name, {1} texture count, {2} the optional "(skipped: n)" tail, {3} the Penumbra group name. "Penumbra" is a plugin name.

Import.Luminis.Result.Ok.Fmt.message: Imported "{0}" — textures: {1}{2}. The glow and the author's own body texture are both on; untick the body under "{3}" in Penumbra if you want the glow by itself.
Import.Luminis.Result.Ok.Fmt.description: Green result line after a successful import. {0} mod folder name, {1} texture count, {2} the optional "(skipped: n)" tail, {3} the Penumbra group name. "Penumbra" is a plugin name.

Import.Luminis.Skip.GamePath.Fmt.message: "{0}" is a real game path, so this is an ordinary TexTools mod rather than an Atramentum Luminis pack. Install it in Penumbra instead.
Import.Luminis.Skip.GamePath.Fmt.description: Why one texture was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …". {0} is the path. It is a real game path, which means the modpack is an ordinary TexTools one. "TexTools" and "Penumbra" are program names. "Atramentum Luminis" is the name of the older FFXIV shader mod these packs were made for; keep it as-is.

Import.Luminis.Skip.Missing.message: the modpack's data blob doesn't contain it.
Import.Luminis.Skip.Missing.description: Why one texture was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. The manifest lists the file but the modpack's data blob does not hold it.

Import.Luminis.Skip.NoGlow.message: its alpha channel is flat, so it carries no glow. Atramentum Luminis puts the glow there, and a texture without one is an ordinary skin rather than a glowing tattoo.
Import.Luminis.Skip.NoGlow.description: Why one texture was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. The texture's alpha channel carries no glow, which is where these packs put it. "Atramentum Luminis" is the name of the older FFXIV shader mod these packs were made for; keep it as-is.

Import.Luminis.Skip.NotATexture.message: it isn't a texture — Atramentum Luminis only carries those.
Import.Luminis.Skip.NotATexture.description: Why one file was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. "Atramentum Luminis" is the name of the older FFXIV shader mod these packs were made for; keep it as-is.

Import.Luminis.Skip.NotTextureData.Fmt.message: it is a model or material (SqPack type {0}), not a texture.
Import.Luminis.Skip.NotTextureData.Fmt.description: Why one file was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. {0} is a numeric file-type code from the game's archive format; "SqPack" is that format's name and is not translated.

Import.Luminis.Skip.Undecodable.description: Why one texture was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. The file is a texture but its pixels would not decode.

Import.Luminis.Skip.UnknownBody.Fmt.message: Proteus doesn't know the body "{0}", and can't ask your character which one they are wearing until they're drawn. Load in and reopen this pack.
Import.Luminis.Skip.UnknownBody.Fmt.description: Why one texture was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …". {0} is the body name the pack used, e.g. "tbse". Proteus normally falls back to the body the character is wearing, and cannot only when the character has not loaded yet.

Import.Luminis.Skip.Unreadable.Fmt.description: Why one texture was skipped, shown as a tooltip. Completes "<file>\nSkipped: …", so it begins in lower case. {0} is the reader's own reason and arrives in English.

Import.Luminis.Warn.FromWearer.Fmt.message: Proteus doesn't know this pack's body layout, so it will paint the art onto the body you're wearing ({0}) exactly as it is, with no resizing. If the pack was painted for a different body it will look wrong — change the body target below if you know better.
Import.Luminis.Warn.FromWearer.Fmt.description: Amber warning in the Import tab. Proteus did not recognise the pack's body, so it will paint the art onto the character's current body with no resizing. {0} is a material file suffix such as "_bibo.mtrl" and must not be translated.

Import.Luminis.Warn.MostlyGlow.Fmt.message: "{0}" glows across {1:P0} of the body. That is legal, but it usually means the texture has no real alpha channel — check the result before wearing it out.
Import.Luminis.Warn.MostlyGlow.Fmt.description: Amber warning in the Import tab. {0} is the texture path, {1} a percentage. Almost the whole body glowing usually means the texture has no real alpha channel rather than a very large tattoo.

Settings.General.AutoRaise.Tip.message:
When another mod is confirmed to be overriding a skin texture Proteus composites
into — a tattoo or skin pack shipping its own copy of the body texture — raise
Proteus' Penumbra priority above it automatically, and say so in chat.

That override is otherwise invisible: overlays half-apply (the bumps land, the
colour doesn't) and every log line still reads as a success.

Turn off only if you deliberately want another mod to win a path Proteus
composites. Proteus never acts on a guess — only on a confirmed override.
Settings.General.AutoRaise.Tip.description: Tooltip and (?) marker. Three paragraphs - keep the blank lines. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.

Settings.General.AutoRedraw.Tip.message:
Let Proteus keep up with the world on its own - recompositing after zoning, gear
changes and redraws, then reloading your character so you can see the result.

Turn it off to make Proteus mostly manual: it won't composite or reload you until
you change something yourself. Your current look stays on either way, and edits
you make still apply - you just won't see them until something redraws you:
zoning, changing gear, or Penumbra's Redraw button.

One exception while it's off: if you're wearing a gear layer, changing gear still
recomposites, so the item hosting that layer doesn't get stranded on something
you took off. You still won't be redrawn for it.

Only covers what Proteus starts. Glamourer's "Auto-Reload Gear" reloads you
whenever any mod's settings change, independently of this.

submesh at a joint (wrist/ankle/…). Some bodies (Neolithe) reinforce joints with a ring
that overlaps an already-complete body; on a sheer overlay the overlap doubles up and
shows as a more-opaque seam. Leave Off for other bodies — there that submesh is real
skin, and hiding it would leave gaps.

Settings.Output.SharpAlpha.Tip.message:
EXPERIMENTAL. Renders shell coverage as a hard alpha-test cutout instead of smooth
transparency, so sphere maps and metalness survive gpose (which drops them on
transparent surfaces). Trade-off: sheer edges become hard/aliased. Best for
mostly-opaque fabrics; a very sheer fabric will look coarse. Recomposite after toggling.
Settings.Output.SharpAlpha.Tip.description: Tooltip and (?) marker. Keep EXPERIMENTAL emphatic. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.

Settings.Output.TextureCache.Tip.message:
How much decoded texture data Proteus keeps in memory between composites.

A 4K texture costs 64 MB decoded, so this is really a count: 2048 MB ≈ 30 of them.
It only helps if it covers a whole composite's worth — below that, every run evicts
what the next one needs and nothing is reused.

Check the "cache N entries, M MB" figure in the recomposite log: if a SECOND
composite with nothing changed still reports misses, raise this. Lower it if the
game starts paging. Released automatically after 60s idle.
Settings.Output.TextureCache.Tip.description: Quotes the literal log line "cache N entries, M MB" - leave that fragment in English, it is what the log actually prints. Contains deliberate line breaks - keep the same number, moving them where your language needs.
